name: Already there
summary: nothing arrives; the first frame is the finished screen
sees: Nothing arrives. The first frame is the finished first screen. The only motion is inside the media: a clip that plays, a product that responds to the pointer, a picture that fades in only if it arrived late.

byImagery.photo: The photograph is there. If none of it had painted by the first frame, it waits on --picture-ground and fades in over 320 ms. A dealt clip plays from frame one, with that frame as its poster.
byImagery.interface: The fragment is HTML and is there at once. Its life is its hover and focus states and any interaction the sheet dealt.
byImagery.type-only: Nothing on the first screen moves.

below.label: Nothing
below.rule: Nothing enters below the fold, and no element on the page gets data-reveal. Section content is simply there, and motion comes from the moves the sheet deals, any moving picture and feedback under the hand. Lazy pictures get the same arrival courtesy as the hero: they wait on their ground colour and fade in when they land. That is loading, not a reveal.

name: Focus pull
summary: the picture racks into focus, then the headline
sees: The first screen comes into focus like a lens finding it. The picture starts soft and a touch large and sharpens over a second; as it does, the headline comes into focus from half strength. Nothing travels, and the sentence and the action are sharp from the first frame.
markup: A photo treatment's filter (black-and-white, a tint) goes on the frame, never on the img or video: the focus animates the picture's own filter.

byImagery.photo: On a phone the picture only settles in scale, with no blur; the headline still comes into focus.
byImagery.interface: The [data-ui] fragment takes the picture's place and comes into focus from 8 px; its labels can be read by about 0.5 s.
byImagery.type-only: Only the headline comes into focus, from half strength; the sentence and the action are there and sharp.

below.label: Headings sharpen
below.rule: Chapter headings (data-reveal="heading", at most one per section) clear from 4 px of blur at 45% strength in 700 ms, once, with no travel. Body copy, pictures, cards and lists never move.

name: Exposure
summary: the photograph's light and colour come up from pale
sees: The type is in place at once. The photograph starts pale, as if over-exposed (dim on a dark page), and its real light and colour come up in about a second.
markup: Use it on a mid-tone or dark photograph: on a pale one the change barely shows and reads as a glitch. A photo treatment's filter goes on the frame, never on the img or video.

byImagery.photo: A photograph or a clip. base.css animates the img's or video's own filter, so a caption in the frame stays at full ink.

below.label: Pictures take their colour
below.rule: Large pictures (data-reveal="picture", four at most) go from 20% saturation to full colour once as they enter, over 900 ms with ease. No travel, no scale, and text never moves.

name: Product at work
summary: the interface ticks, draws, lands a row and selects one
sees: The interface is complete and readable at the first frame, then shows it is live in four short steps: the key figure ticks up to its value, the chart's latest stretch draws in, the newest row lands as the rows below make room, and one row becomes selected. The headline, sentence and action never move.
markup: Inside the `[data-ui]` fragment: `data-e="figure"` with `data-roll` on the key figure (only its last two digits move), `data-e="chart"` on the chart, `data-e="new-row"` on the newest row (its slot already in the layout; set `--ui-row-gap` on the fragment to the list's row gap), `data-e="select"` on the row that becomes selected (its own style is the selected one; put the unselected colours in `--ui-row-bg` and `--ui-row-ink` on the fragment). Leave out any marker the fragment has no part for. Run the Rolling figures script (motion.md) and the chart call inline right after the fragment, never on load. base.js holds the moments of a fragment that starts low on a phone until it is in view.

byImagery.interface: The fragment is the picture. Mark the figure, the chart, the newest row and the selected row inside it, and leave out the marker for any part the fragment does not have.

below.label: Interface only
below.rule: Each further [data-ui] fragment (data-reveal="ui") except the product replay (data-replay, which plays its own beats) plays one data moment once as it enters: its chart draws (data-moment="chart"), its newest row lands (data-moment="row"), or its figure rolls (data-roll, the Rolling figures recipe). One per fragment. Headings, text and photographs never move.

name: Aperture
summary: the picture opens from a small window out past its edges
sees: The picture opens from a small window in its middle out past every edge of its frame, pulling back from a detail to the whole view. The type is in place from the first frame and never moves.
markup: Centre the window on the subject with `--window: <top> <right> <bottom> <left>` on the frame (default `34% 36%`); on an interface fragment also `--from-scale: 1.1`.

byImagery.photo: As described; centre the window on the subject with four insets.
byImagery.interface: The window opens on the fragment's key figure or selected row. Set --from-scale: 1.1 so its text is never more than 10% too large.

below.label: Pictures open from a window
below.rule: Up to three large pictures (data-reveal="picture") open once from a centred window (inset 12% 14%) while the photograph eases back from 1.08, over 1,000 ms. Text never moves.

name: Set type
summary: headline lines rise from masks; the picture opens like a blind
sees: The headline's lines rise out of their own baselines one after another while the picture opens downward like a blind; the sentence and the action rise 12 px after them.
markup: Wrap each headline line: `…`, three at most, with breaks that fit on one line at every width down to 360 px (a smaller display step on phones if they must).

byImagery.interface: The frame opens over the fragment, and the fragment settles from 1.08.
byImagery.type-only: Lines, then sentence and action; there is no picture step.

below.label: Headings by line
below.rule: Chapter headings (data-lines, five at most) rise line by line from their masks once, using the "Lines that rise on scroll" script in motion.md. Nothing else enters, and a stray data-reveal does nothing.

name: Line blocks
summary: solid blocks slide off each headline line
sees: Each line of the headline starts as a solid block of one palette colour, exactly as long as its words, and the blocks slide off toward the line ends one after another. The words never move.
markup: Wrap each headline line: `…`, three at most, with breaks that fit on one line at every width down to 360 px (a smaller display step on phones if they must): a line that wraps gets one block across the whole column, and the inspector fails it.

byImagery.photo: The picture is in place and still.
byImagery.interface: The fragment is in place and still.
byImagery.type-only: The natural fit: before the words appear, the blocks are the only shapes on the first screen.

below.label: Rows step in
below.rule: Lists, indexes, tables and price rows (data-reveal="rows" on the list) go from 40% to full opacity in reading order, once: the first four 60 ms apart, the rest together. No travel, nothing else enters, and no blocks below the fold.
